authors: John J. O'Neill | Trevor K. Stephens | Timothy M. Kowalewski
title: Evaluation of Torque Measurement Surrogates as Applied to Grip Torque and Jaw Angle Estimation of Robotic Surgical Tools
version: IEEE RA-L published version, vol. 3(4), 3027–3034; online June 22, 2018
locator: II.A and Figure 1/2, III.B and Table III, Acknowledgment and References 11, 12, 15
evidence: A common 1 kHz microcontroller samples independent proximal and distal FUTEK TFF325 sensors, motor current and commands. For end-to-end estimation the measured study result using the motor command was 4.42 mN·m RMSE; supplying proximal torque sensing gave 1.78 mN·m.
rights_and_limitations: IEEE retained copyright; personal use in author-hosted publisher PDF. The models are tested on bench data; neither prediction error establishes operation at a current limit.

authors: Nathan J. Kong | Trevor K. Stephens | John J. O’Neill | Timothy M. Kowalewski
title: Design of a Portable Dynamic Calibration Instrument for daVinci Si Tools
version: 2017 ASME Design of Medical Devices Conference; author-hosted proceedings PDF
evidence: Describes the precursor calibration mechanism. The jaw and torque transducer are fixed on a common axis. Current feedback sets resistance; 10 and 35 mN·m tests cross 0.1/0.5 Hz and all channels are sampled synchronously at 1 kHz.
rights_and_limitations: ASME retained copyright. This methods paper specifies its own four conditions and does not label every archived 2018 experiment.

authors: Yangming Li | Muneaki Miyasaka | Mohammad Haghighipanah | Lei Cheng | Blake Hannaford
title: Dynamic modeling of cable driven elongated surgical instruments for sensorless grip force estimation
locator: Experiment on Raven-II/10 mm gripper, Fig. 11; PubMed 34290900
evidence: Uses a cable transmission model and an unscented Kalman filter. Independent one-dimensional jaw force sensors check predictions from motor torque and encoders; free-motion residuals are evaluated separately.
rights_and_limitations: Public author manuscript. No robot file was downloaded from this work, and the independent output is force at a jaw.

title: Gaussian Process Regression for Sensorless Grip Force Estimation of Cable-Driven Elongated Surgical Instruments
evidence: Four Gaussian-process estimators and a dynamic-model filter are compared on a real Raven-II gripper using measured grip force. The simpler two-input GPR performed best among the four in this study.
rights_and_limitations: Public author manuscript. Its PMC bibliography hyperlinks multiple distinct 2016 conference papers to the same DOI; the titles were resolved independently below.

authors: Muneaki Miyasaka | Mohammad Haghighipanah | Yangming Li | Blake Hannaford
title: Hysteresis model of longitudinally loaded cable for cable driven robots and identification of the parameters
version: 2016 ICRA publisher abstract and Crossref work metadata
locator: Publisher abstract; Li and Hannaford (2017), reference 14
evidence: Reports a cable longitudinal hysteresis model identified from experimental behavior, a mechanical source of discrepancy between motor and load.
rights_and_limitations: Metadata and abstract screened. No numeric file or full-text verification claimed.

authors: Mohammad Haghighipanah | Muneaki Miyasaka | Yangming Li | Blake Hannaford
title: Unscented Kalman Filter and 3D vision to improve cable driven surgical robot joint angle estimation
version: 2016 ICRA proceedings, NSF Public Access Repository copy
locator: §V–VI, Experiment C, Fig. 8–12 and Table I, camera-occlusion subsection
evidence: The authors check UKF and transmission-kinematics joint-angle estimates against attached joint encoders on six trajectories. For trials of simulated camera occlusion, camera observations were removed for repeated two-second intervals.
rights_and_limitations: IEEE publisher terms shown in the accessible PDF. The measured reference is joint angle. No independently measured shaft torque or force traces were downloaded.
